items.title: Norris takes pole; official grid confirms penalty-adjusted order
items.summary: Formula1.com's official 22-car Qualifying result and FIA Document 50's final classification agree: Lando Norris took pole in 1:27.470, 0.204s ahead of George Russell, with Kimi Antonelli third. The official Starting Grid now lists all 22 entrants after penalties, including Russell seventh, Leclerc 14th, Hamilton 20th, Verstappen 21st and Perez 22nd.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the FIA/Formula1.com qualifying classification distinct from the penalty-adjusted official grid. The Race's earlier post-penalty order was provisional and is no longer needed to fill an unavailable-results gap.

items.title: Hamilton's cumulative 75-place penalty; Verstappen targets a fun recovery
items.summary: FIA Documents 42–43 add 65 places to Hamilton's earlier 10-place drop; he qualified 11th and the official Starting Grid lists him 20th. Verstappen's FIA Document 33 imposes a 30-place drop, and the 22-car official grid lists him 21st.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the component sanctions and qualifying classification distinct from the penalty-adjusted official grid; the grid, rather than the earlier provisional order, confirms Hamilton and Verstappen's starting positions.

items.title: Perez receives a formal warning after discarding a loose cockpit item
items.summary: FIA Document 40 resolves the FP3 unsafe-condition summons in Document 31. After reviewing in-car video, the Stewards found that Perez threw a small plastic cable organiser, which had detached from the seat belt, out of the car. Cadillac received a formal warning: throwing material onto the track during a live session was inappropriate even though this small, light item was unlikely to damage another car or injure a driver.
items.why_it_matters: The warning follows a safety-related finding, but is not a grid penalty. Keep it separate from Perez's 30-place power-unit sanction in Document 39.

items.title: Mercedes can clinch the constructors' title with a three-point gain
items.summary: The latest official standings show Mercedes on 630 points, 126 ahead of Ferrari on 504. Formula1.com's pre-weekend scenario says Mercedes clinches the constructors' title if it gains three points on Ferrari in Brazil. No Brazil points have been awarded yet.
items.why_it_matters: Kimi Antonelli has clinched the Drivers' title, while the Constructors' Championship remains live; the three-point threshold depends on the Race result.

items.title: Bearman reprimanded for reversing in the pit lane
items.summary: FIA Document 41 identifies Oliver Bearman (Car 87, TGR Haas F1 Team) and says he reversed in the pit lane under his own power during Qualifying, breaching Article B1.6.3b. The Stewards imposed a driving reprimand, his second of the season; the document states no grid drop.
items.why_it_matters: This is a new qualifying ruling, but a reprimand rather than a grid penalty. Keep it separate from the still-unpublished qualifying order.
